question: Whether to approve Georgia Power's proposed FCR-27 fuel cost recovery rates for June 2026 through May 2028, along with its requested changes to the interim fuel rider threshold and its natural gas hedging program.

outcome.summary: The Commission adopted the Staff–Georgia Power stipulation: FCR-27 rates effective for bills from June 1, 2026, a $13.0 million fuel balance reduction, hedging limited to 20% of budgeted gas burn over 36 months, and a $300 million IFR threshold with a required rate proposal. It ordered an RTP fuel credit review by December 31, 2026, and rejected the $152 million disallowance and other intervenor proposals.

positions.asked: Asks approval of its FCR-27 application as modified by its stipulation with Staff, without changes: a $13 million fuel balance reduction, $300 million IFR threshold, hedging capped at 20% over 36 months; and rejection of intervenors' fuel cost sharing and $152 million coal disallowance.

notes: Georgia Power's original application (Houston/Berrigan testimony, doc 225466) asked for a 12.6% FCR decrease ($5.74/month for a 1,000 kWh residential customer), an IFR threshold increase from $200 million to $300 million, and hedging expanded from 40% over 36 months to 60% over 48 months; its brief instead asks for approval as modified by the stipulation; The stipulation's own text is not in our files (doc 226544 file 107826 is only Staff's cover letter; updated stipulation doc 226572 has no text; docs 226745/226747 show only transmittals and the RSM signature page), so stipulation terms are taken from Georgia Power's brief, Staff's proposed order and the Commission's order; Sierra Club entry is the joint brief of Sierra Club, SACE and NRDC (intervened as 'Southern Alliance for Clean Energy, Sierra Club, NRDC', doc 225480); it also asks that the stipulation's 15% cap on above-market coal purchases be lowered to 0-5% and, alternatively to the disallowance, limits on coal contracts with minimum-delivery penalties and fixes to load and solar forecast biases. Stance 'opposes company request' is a judgment call: it supports the stipulation's hedging and RTP paragraphs; GIPL/Southface's brief supports the stipulation's fuel terms; the Commission's order instead describes Lin's earlier testimony (keep the $200 million IFR threshold, cut the adjustment cap to 15%, add a fuel line item to bills). The brief says it still favors smaller adjustments and the bill line item, and that it may recommend changes to the settlement later; GAM's testimony (Pollock, doc 226169) opposed the hedging expansion and argued 45U nuclear tax credits should offset fuel costs; per Staff's proposed order, the stipulation instead applied more credits to the storm docket. Its last word is the support letter; MARTA's May 14 brief (doc 226582) has no text; its entry rests on its later joinder to the stipulation; RSM filed no brief or testimony we could read; its entry rests only on its joinder; Georgia WAND filed a late intervention (May 4, 2026) with no stated ask; the order says it did not show good cause, and Georgia Power's brief says it did not take part in the hearings; The order filed Aug 4, 2026 says it reflects action taken May 28, 2026 (short order doc 226750); Staff's proposed order lists Feb 28, 2026 as the FCR-28 filing date, apparently a typo for the Feb 28, 2029 date in the stipulation and the order; Other questions: the stipulation also settles Georgia Power's storm damage recovery case (Docket 44280); the RTP fuel credit methodology review ordered under ordering paragraph 6 remains open in this docket through December 31, 2026 and is not covered here
